title: State Entropy Regularization for Robust Reinforcement Learning

predicted_errors.error_location: Preliminaries definition of d_P^π; Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines d_P^π(s) = Σ_{t=0}^∞ γ^t Pr(s_t=s), whose total mass is 1/(1-γ), not 1. Nevertheless it repeatedly treats d_P^π as a probability distribution: entropy H_S(d_P^π) is applied to it, Eq. (12) states that d^π and softmax are both probability vectors and therefore λ*=1, and the proof invokes the entropy/LSE convex-conjugacy valid on the simplex. These steps are invalid under the paper's own discounted-occupancy definition unless d is normalized, e.g. by multiplying by 1-γ. This affects the central reward-robustness theorem, all table guarantees, and subsequent kernel results.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 3.1, Table 1, and Appendix A.1 worst-case reward
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For the stated uncertainty constraint LSE_S((r^π-tilde r^π)/α) ≤ ε/α + log S, assuming normalized d, stationarity gives Δr^π(s)=α log d^π(s)+C and constraint saturation requires C=ε+α log S. Thus an action-independent adversarial reward is tilde r(s,a)=r(s,a)-α log d^π(s)-ε-α log S. The paper instead gives r(s,a)-α log d^π(s)-ε. That proposed reward has LSE equal to ε/α rather than ε/α+log S and does not attain the claimed robust value E[r]-ε+α(H(d)-log S). The displayed adversarial reward and the robust-return formula are therefore mutually inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 3.1 claim for 'any π' and its asserted worst-case reward
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: No full-support assumption on d_P^π is made. For ordinary policies many states have d_P^π(s)=0, but the purported adversarial reward contains -α log d_P^π(s), which is infinite. Correspondingly, softmax in Eq. (12) cannot equal a distribution with zero entries at a finite optimizer. Therefore the claimed finite worst-case reward and attained KKT solution do not hold 'for any π' as stated; the result would need a full-support condition or a limiting/supremum formulation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, especially the claim that state entropy 'exactly solves a reward-robust RL problem'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The uncertainty set in Theorem 3.1 is explicitly policy dependent, \tilde{R}^π(ε,α), through r^π and d_P^π. The theorem only establishes a pointwise identity after fixing π. It does not establish equivalence to the conventional robust-RL optimization max_π min_{r∈R} J(π,P,r) with one policy-independent uncertainty set R, as defined in the paper's Preliminaries. Calling this an exact solution of a reward-robust RL problem without prominently qualifying the decision-dependent uncertainty set overstates what is proved.

The purported kernel-robustness proof changes the probability measure without justification. Eq. (28) contains E_{ρ_P^π}[log \tilde{ρ}_P^π], but Eq. (31) replaces this with min_{\tilde P} E_{ρ_{\tilde P}^π}[log ρ_{\tilde P}^π]. These are different quantities and neither importance sampling nor containment of uncertainty sets permits that substitution. Eq. (33 likewise changes the fixed term E_{ρ_P^π}[log r] from Eq. (28) into min_{\tilde P}E_{ρ_{\tilde P}^π}[log r]. Consequently the claimed lower bound does not follow. In addition, Eq. (26) requires absolute continuity of occupancies and positivity of r for logarithms, neither of which is included in the theorem statement.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2 and Appendix A.6, Eq. (41) CVaR definition
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says CVaR_β is the expected return in the worst β-fraction of outcomes, but Eq. (41) defines min_η {η + [1/(1-β)]E[(R-η)^+]}. That is the standard upper-tail CVaR construction for a loss/random variable convention, not lower-tail ('worst return') CVaR as claimed. A lower-tail return CVaR instead involves, for example, max_η {η - β^{-1}E[(η-R)^+]}. The later dual representation uses a density bound 1/β, which corresponds to a lower-tail quantity and is inconsistent with Eq. (41)'s 1/(1-β) upper-tail formula. Therefore Theorem 4.2 is not proved for the objective the paper defines.

With the paper's own unnormalized discounted occupancy, a constant per-step reward r=c has J(π,P,r)=Σ_t γ^t c=c/(1-γ), not c. Eq. (39) asserts min_{\tilde P}E_{ρ_{\tilde P}^π}[r]=c. Although a corrected constant factor would still support a version of the contradiction argument, the displayed proof is mathematically false under the stated definitions.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5 rollout-budget and temperature paragraphs versus Figure 5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Figure 5 labels panel (b) 'Reward Shift,' panel (c) 'Rollouts Per Entropy Estimation Ablation,' and panel (d) 'Varying Regularization Strengths.' Yet the rollout-budget discussion says 'Figure 5(b) shows' rollout counts of 4, 20, and 50, and the temperature discussion says robustness is shown in 'Figure 5(c).' These references are swapped and direct readers to figures that do not display the described experiments, impairing verification of the empirical claims.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction citation [6] and Section 5 'PR-MDP and NR-MDP frameworks [6]'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference [6] is Chen et al. (2019), 'Top-K off-policy correction for a REINFORCE recommender system.' It is neither a PR-MDP/NR-MDP robust-control paper nor an appropriate citation for the claimed robust action-adversary frameworks. The same reference is also used in the introductory list of major RL successes, despite being a recommender-system correction paper. The robust-baseline attribution is demonstrably wrong; relevant action-adversarial robust RL work is instead associated with papers such as Pinto et al. (2017), which the bibliography lists separately as [47].

The corollaries assume an empirical distribution \hat d and compare it in L1 to d_P^π, then apply entropy continuity bounds for two probability distributions. But d_P^π was defined earlier as an unnormalized discounted occupancy with mass 1/(1-γ). Thus the assumed L1 comparison and entropy continuity argument are not valid as written. These corollaries inherit the normalization defect of Theorem 3.1 rather than providing valid finite-sample guarantees.
